algorithms.title: Triage Officer Action Card
algorithms.description: Put on the vest. Grab tags. Go.
steps: Report to IC; get the area to triage and your team (pairs).
Global sort: 'If you can walk, go to [point]' → 'Wave if you need help'.
Systematic sweep (e.g., clockwise / row by row); START/JumpSTART or SALT per local protocol.
Seconds-long LSIs only: tourniquet/pressure, open airway/position, (child) breaths per protocol, auto-injector.
Tag every patient; mark searched areas.
Report counts by category to IC (red/yellow/green/black) and update as they change.
Direct litter teams: reds to treatment area first.
Re-triage; hand the dead to the morgue manager.

algorithms.title: Transport Officer Action Card
algorithms.description: You move patients and paperwork, not stretchers.
steps: Set up the ambulance loading zone (one-way flow, close to treatment area exit).
Get hospital capacity/capability through Med Comms or the hospital coordination center.
Request units from Staging as patients are ready.
Assign destination by category + hospital capability (trauma, burns, peds) — spread the load.
Load reds first; use buses (with medic) for greens; avoid 'one patient per ambulance' if yellows/greens can share.
Log: tag # · category · unit · destination · time.
Update IC with patients transported/remaining.

algorithms.title: Treatment Officer Action Card
algorithms.description: Keep them alive and keep them moving.
steps: Choose the treatment area: safe, upwind, near the loading zone, room to expand, one entrance/one exit.
Lay out red / yellow / green zones (tarps/flags) with a separate, out-of-view black area.
Assign Red, Yellow, Green treatment managers.
Secondary triage at the entrance; re-triage regularly.
Focused care: airway, O2, bleeding, splinting, warmth; minimal procedures that don't slow flow.
Prioritize patients for the Transport Officer; request supplies via Logistics.
